headline: Showers are ending and Tuesday turns sunny but cool and windy; after a dry Wednesday, the next storm brings rain, wind and a slight chance of thunderstorms on Thursday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: The last showers end around sunrise Tuesday, and the day turns mostly sunny but cool and breezy, with highs in the upper 60s along the coast and valleys, lower 70s in the low desert, 50s in the High Desert and upper 30s to lower 50s in the mountains, roughly 2–12 degrees below normal. Winds peak around midday: the San Diego County coast sees occasional gusts near 20 knots (about 25 mph) into the afternoon, while mountains and deserts gust 25–40 mph, topping 40 mph on ridges and through passes with very isolated gusts near 50 mph. Winds ease late Tuesday afternoon and evening, and clouds drift back over the coast Tuesday night, with a small (10–20%) chance of a low cloud deck early Wednesday morning.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Wednesday is mostly sunny, dry and not windy, but only a couple of degrees warmer. The next storm arrives Thursday morning in Orange and western San Bernardino Counties and spreads southeast through the day, bringing rain, a slight chance of thunderstorms, and gusts of 35–50 mph in the mountains and deserts. By the time it moves out early Friday, totals should be a little over an inch in the mountains, under three-quarters of an inch for most of San Diego and Riverside Counties, and perhaps only about a quarter inch around San Diego. Snow levels drop to around 6,500 feet as the rain ends, giving Big Bear light snow and a few inches above 7,500 feet such as the higher ski slopes; Friday afternoon then turns fair and dry.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Saturday looks fair and dry. Sunday and Monday are very uncertain: it could stay dry, but most computer-model runs bring in a weak system with light rain sometime Sunday, Sunday night or Monday. After that, some runs build a strong area of high pressure over the West that would bring dry and very warm weather ahead of Thanksgiving, while others keep the cool, unsettled and sometimes wet and windy pattern going.

coast: A High Surf Advisory is in effect until 4 AM Wednesday for the Orange County and San Diego County coasts: surf of 6–9 feet with sets to 11 feet on west-facing beaches, plus strong rip currents through midweek. Surf dips briefly to 3–5 feet with sets to 6 feet on Wednesday, then a new northwest swell raises it again Thursday through Friday. Minor coastal flooding is expected at times during high tides this week because of the surf, even with tides under 6.5 feet through Friday; King Tides peak next week, with tides over 7 feet possible starting Saturday, Nov. 21. For boaters, a Small Craft Advisory runs until 4 AM Wednesday with 25–30 knot gusts (near gale force around San Clemente Island) and steep 7–10 ft seas, easing Wednesday morning, before steep 7–10 ft seas and 20–30 knot gusts return Thursday into Friday morning.
watch_for: Thursday's rain amounts around San Diego, which may be only about a quarter inch while areas to the north get more.
High surf and minor coastal flooding at high tide, with King Tides starting to push above 7 feet from Saturday.
Whether Sunday–Monday brings light rain, and whether a warm, dry spell follows before Thanksgiving.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in a sunny, breezy Tuesday and a dry Wednesday, more confident than before in Thursday's storm details, and quite uncertain about Sunday onward.
